features.feature_value: They decided based on whether the content had factual support and debate value vs being merely inflammatory/ill-informed.
features.evidence_span: evaluated whether they had any factual basis and debate/discusion value or were merely inflammatory and ill informed
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly describes criteria of factual basis and discussion value versus inflammatory misinformation.

features.feature_value: They felt removal/should-not-allow when posts threatened or used personal attacks with profanity.
features.evidence_span: posed a threat and used personal attacks that used profanity
features.rationale: The participant ties allowance to absence of threats and profanity-laden personal attacks.

features.feature_value: Expletives are unnecessary and increase perceived vitriol, influencing the decision.
features.evidence_span: the use of expletives is unnecessary and injects a level of vitriol
features.rationale: They cite expletives as the cue that makes discourse more vitriolic, affecting approval/removal.

features.feature_value: They disliked name-calling, which influenced whether to approve/remove.
features.rationale: The reflection directly attributes influence to aversion to name calling.

features.feature_value: They tried to determine whether the stance was elaborated/irrational and whether it suggested resorting to violence.
features.evidence_span: check if they were suggesting resorting to violence
features.rationale: The participant’s stated evaluation includes checking for violence and assessing reasoning quality.

features.feature_value: Allowed if it furthers conversation and is not offensive/derogatory in a personal sense.
features.evidence_span: furthers conversation without being offensive in a personal sense or derogatory
features.rationale: They specify an acceptability rule centered on conversational value and lack of personal derogation.

features.feature_value: They attempted to remove clearly false things while generally thinking most content should be allowed.
features.evidence_span: I tried to remove clearly false things.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states their removal target as clearly false information.

features.feature_value: They interpreted the pair as similar to real social media debate; they allowed rude/accusatory content as part of online debate as long as it didn't cross a line.
features.evidence_span: Some were rude and accusatory but that should be allowed in an online debate.
features.rationale: The reflection emphasizes comparing to real conversational patterns and concludes that rudeness/accusations were still acceptable.
